featured.takeaway: Treat tagged animals as interacting particles and train a graph-network simulator on bio-logger and drone tracks to predict how groups move; a tag could then send only where its animal departs from the prediction, cutting the data it has to transmit.
featured.whyFeatured: Highest rating of all 88 runs (8.1) and the only one above 7.8, with claim risk 0.25; its novelty is the highest yet. It is one run and was not re-run: batch 3's re-runs showed that a single rating can be off by about a point either way.

featured.takeaway: Pretrain a music transcription model on unlabelled audio the way wav2vec 2.0 learns speech, by masking parts of the signal, then fine-tune it on the few labelled recordings; the gain may be largest for instruments with little labelled data, such as guitar.
featured.whyFeatured: Best of the music runs (6.9, eighth of 88; claim risk 0.25). It builds on a reported result, MT3's large gains on small datasets such as GuitarSet and URMP; the validator marks the claim extrapolated, not grounded, because the reason it gives is not in the papers.

featured.takeaway: Run animal-call detectors on neuromorphic chips inside battery-powered field recorders so they can listen all the time; but the validator flags as risky the claim that this ends a trade-off between detection sensitivity and battery life that neither field has solved.
featured.whyFeatured: Shows that the two checks are separate: the judge model rated it as plausible and coherent as E5 (0.72 and 0.78), yet the validator marks its last sentence risky (0.72), because the passages discuss low-power chips and battery limits separately and none says the trade-off is unsolved. Rated 5.8, 48th of 88.
